subject: Request: One-off POC credit allotment + 30d sandbox extension for Auralis Health
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: One-off POC credit allotment + 30d sandbox extension for Auralis Health

Hi team,

Quick summary: Auralis (healthcare analytics startup) is mid-demo and has hit a regulatory testing block — they need an additional 30 days on the sandbox and a one-time allotment of platform credits to complete an expanded clinical data ingestion test. Their procurement deadline is 9/15; if we don't give them more runway they will likely pause and re-evaluate other vendors.

Why this matters: Maria (Head of AI) is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile on private deployments. The customer is explicitly evaluating a private VPC deployment and we are the only vendor that has cleared their initial compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence attached). This POC is high-touch but could convert to a committed dedicated deployment with multi-year ARR potential (estimated $650k ARR first 18 months).

Ask: Executive approval to grant a one-time credit of 60,000 token-equivalent credits (approx. $8k list value) and a 30-day sandbox extension beyond our standard PLG 14-day cap. Terms proposed below.

Proposed guardrails (recommended):
- One-time credit only, expires if no signed committment within 90 days after the extended POC.
- Require signed addendum (DocuSign) that caps scope to the POC and enables audit logging for the sandbox environment.
- Enable private deployment preview only if legal signs mutual NDA addendum (we can share template).

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf (summary of SOC2 artifacts we shared), auralis-poc-plan.xlsx (detailed tests they need).

I'm asking for a quick decision today so we can send procurement a single email with terms.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: soc2-summary.pdf (pdf, 420 KB)]
[Attachment: auralis-poc-plan.xlsx (xlsx, 220 KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC credit allotment + 30d sandbox extension for Auralis Health

Kim — fully support. A few datapoints for context:
- Auralis passed the first-phase security review and indicated they will fast-track procurement once the extended ingest tests are green.
- There's a downstream pilot with their payer-partner that could add another $300k ARR in year two if the demo validates.
- They asked specifically for a 30d stability window for large batch replays and a few more KV-cache capacity hours; the requested credit hits exactly the token burn they expect for those replays.

Suggested additional condition: require feature-flagged throttles so the POC token usage is capped to the allotment and can't be exceeded without an explicit credit top-up request. That avoids surprises and keeps finance happy.

If approved, I will: 1) update the HubSpot deal record (link below), 2) send the DocuSign addendum + usage cap language, 3) confirm a scheduled check-in with Maria at the 2-week mark.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/DEAL-9842-AUR

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Revenue Operations
[Note: Proposed addendum attached below in Kimberly's draft]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC credit allotment + 30d sandbox extension for Auralis Health

Thanks for the clear ask and attachments, Kim. Recommendation: approve the one-time credit + 30d extension with the following executive conditions:
1) Finance sign-off (Rishi) for the credit amount and a line-item in our specials ledger.
2) Legal to attach the proposed-addendum.docx via DocuSign; add a clause that any production rollout must include an SOW and committed spend within 90 days.
3) Implement Aditya's usage cap and feature-flag so the POC cannot burn beyond the approved allotment.

This is strategically aligned and low risk given the compliance materials. If Rishi signs off, we can commit immediately and I will ask CX to schedule a dedicated engineer for the last two weeks of the extension.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales — Midmarket
Redwood Inference

On the 90-day clause — aim for a clear conversion milestone (PO signed or negotiated term sheet).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: One-off POC credit allotment + 30d sandbox extension for Auralis Health

Approved — one-time exception granted with conditions.

Approval details:
- Credit: 60,000 token-equivalent credits (internal value ~ $8,000) applied to DEAL-9842-AUR.
- Sandbox extension: +30 calendar days, effective from the day we grant access.

Executive conditions (must be completed before credits are enabled):
1) DocuSign addendum signed by Auralis procurement (use proposed-addendum.docx). Addendum must include: usage cap, scope limited to POC artifacts, and a 90-day conversion milestone.
2) Engineering to enable a hard usage cap/feature-flag tied to the credit allotment — no auto-topups. (Aditya, please coordinate with infra.)
3) Enable audit logging on the sandbox environment for the POC and forward logs to our legal hold for six months.
4) Finance will mark this as a one-off promotion; if usage exceeds the allotment and customer requests additional credits, those must go through Deal Desk.

Aditya — once DocuSign is returned, instruct ops to flip the flag and notify procurement. Kimberly — please confirm you will ask Maria to sign the addendum and send a single-threaded DocuSign link.

Rishi Malhotra
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-addendum.docx (docx, 34 KB)]
